name: Olfactory Context and Affective Memory
higher_order_principle: Olfactory signals project directly to amygdala and hippocampus (bypassing thalamus), resulting in rapid, non-suppressible hedonic evaluation and powerful context-memory binding ('Proust effect'). Olfactory signatures form persistent, emotionally charged environmental memories.
scope_conditions: Requires functioning olfactory system (anosmia eliminates effect)
Adaptation is rapid (conscious awareness fades in minutes), but subconscious effects persist
moderators: context_congruency (does the smell fit the visual scene?)

interactions.description: Olfactory context is a potent cue for the spatial context memory system.

key_references: Herz & Schooler (2002) American Journal of Psychology
